title: That Fluffy Cloud Above You Weighs a Million Pounds

scenes.text: That fluffy cloud above you weighs more than a million pounds.
Scientists measured it. A normal cumulus cloud holds about half a gram of water in every cubic metre.
Sounds tiny. But that cloud is a kilometre wide, a kilometre long and a kilometre tall.
Add it up and you get five hundred thousand kilograms of water. Heavier than a fully loaded jumbo jet.
It floats because that weight is spread across trillions of droplets so small the slightest breeze keeps them up.
So next time you lie on the grass watching clouds, remember what is hanging over your head. What should I weigh next?

description:
The fluffy cumulus cloud drifting above you weighs around 1.1 million pounds, about 500,000 kilograms.
A typical cumulus cloud holds about half a gram of water per cubic metre, but it is roughly a kilometre on each side, so the water adds up to more than a fully loaded jumbo jet.
It stays up because that weight is spread across trillions of tiny droplets that even the lightest breeze can carry.
What everyday thing should I weigh next?
